title: Mathematics
blurb: From fractions and negatives to derivatives and integrals, one step at a time.
intro: The full path from middle-school number sense to AP Calculus. Each unit builds on the last, so go in order. Every lesson has worked examples and practice you type answers into.

units.title: Number Sense
units.summary: Negatives, fractions, decimals, percents and ratios: the tools everything else uses.

lessons.title: Integers and negative numbers
lessons.desc: Numbers below zero follow a few simple rules. Learn them once and you'll never second-guess a sign again.

lessons.title: Fractions: the complete toolkit
lessons.desc: Simplifying, adding, multiplying and dividing fractions, plus why each rule works.

lessons.title: Decimals and percents
lessons.desc: Converting between fractions, decimals and percents, and the multiplier trick for any price change.

lessons.title: Ratios, rates and unit rates
lessons.desc: Comparing quantities, finding the better deal, and converting units without memorizing anything.

lessons.title: Proportions and scaling
lessons.desc: When two quantities grow together at a fixed rate, and how to spot when they don't.

units.title: Expressions & Equations
units.summary: Using letters for unknowns and solving for them.

lessons.title: Variables and expressions
lessons.desc: Letters stand for numbers you don't know yet. Here's how to write, simplify and evaluate expressions.

lessons.title: Solving one- and two-step equations
lessons.desc: An equation is a balance. Whatever you do to one side, do to the other, and the unknown falls out.

lessons.title: Multi-step equations
lessons.desc: Variables on both sides, parentheses and fractions: one clean process handles them all.

lessons.title: Inequalities
lessons.desc: Solving for a range of answers instead of one, and the one rule that trips everyone up.

lessons.title: Exponents and scientific notation
lessons.desc: Repeated multiplication, the exponent rules, and how scientists write huge and tiny numbers.

lessons.title: Square roots and irrational numbers
lessons.desc: Undoing a square, estimating roots in your head, and the numbers that never end.

units.title: Geometry Foundations
units.summary: Angles, area, volume and the Pythagorean theorem.

lessons.title: Angles and lines
lessons.desc: Angles are measured turns. A handful of rules about straight lines and parallel lines solve most angle puzzles.

lessons.title: Area and perimeter
lessons.desc: Perimeter is the fence; area is the grass. Learn the core formulas and the trick for odd shapes.

lessons.title: Circles and pi
lessons.desc: Every circle hides the same number, π. With it you can find any circle's distance around and area.

lessons.title: Volume and surface area
lessons.desc: Volume is how much a box holds; surface area is how much cardboard it takes. Prisms, cylinders, cones and spheres.

lessons.title: The Pythagorean theorem
lessons.desc: In every right triangle, a² + b² = c². It lets you find any distance you can't measure directly.

units.title: Statistics & Probability
units.summary: Summarizing data and measuring chance.

lessons.title: Mean, median, mode and range
lessons.desc: One number to describe the middle of your data, another to describe how spread out it is, and why picking the wrong one lets people lie with true numbers.

lessons.title: Reading and making data displays
lessons.desc: Which chart fits which data, how to read box plots and scatter plots in seconds, and how to catch a graph that's lying to you.

lessons.title: Probability basics
lessons.desc: Probability is the math of uncertainty. Learn to count outcomes, tell theory from experience, and spot the gambler's fallacy, the most expensive mistake in trading.

lessons.title: Compound probability and expected value
lessons.desc: And, or, at least one, and what you can expect to win or lose on average. The math casinos, insurers and professional traders live by.

units.title: Algebra 1
units.summary: Linear functions, systems, polynomials and quadratics.

lessons.title: Functions and slope
lessons.desc: A function is a rule that turns each input into exactly one output. Slope measures how fast the output changes. Together they describe pay rates, fuel costs and every trend line on a chart.

lessons.title: Writing linear equations
lessons.desc: Turn a graph, two points or a real situation into an equation you can use to predict, compare and decide.

lessons.title: Systems of equations
lessons.desc: Two equations, two unknowns, one answer that works for both. The tool for break-even points, comparing offers and solving any problem with two moving parts.

lessons.title: Polynomials
lessons.desc: Expressions built from terms like 3x², −5x and 7. How to add, subtract and multiply them, and the one squaring mistake almost everyone makes.

lessons.title: Factoring
lessons.desc: Multiplying runs forward; factoring runs it backward. It's the key that unlocks quadratic equations, and a checklist makes it routine.

lessons.title: Quadratic equations
lessons.desc: Equations with x². Four ways to solve them, a formula that always works, and the parabola that describes everything thrown, jumped or launched.

lessons.title: Exponential growth and decay
lessons.desc: Linear adds the same amount every step. Exponential multiplies. Compound interest, debt, depreciation, viral spread, and why a 50% loss needs a 100% gain to recover.

units.title: Geometry
units.summary: Proof, similarity and right-triangle trigonometry.

units.title: Algebra 2
units.summary: Function families, logarithms and sequences.

units.title: Precalculus
units.summary: The unit circle, trig identities and the idea of a limit.

units.title: AP Calculus AB
units.summary: The eight units of the AP Calculus AB course, in College Board order.

lessons.title: Chain rule, implicit and inverse functions

title: Vocabulary
blurb: Roots, context clues and 600+ words that sharpen how you read, write and talk.
intro: Vocabulary is the fastest way to grow crystallized knowledge. You'll learn how words are built so you can decode new ones, then work through word sets by level.

units.title: How Words Work
units.summary: The decoding toolkit: context, prefixes, suffixes and roots.

lessons.title: Context clues
lessons.desc: Most new words come with hints sitting right next to them. Here's how to read the hints.

lessons.title: Prefixes that flip meaning
lessons.desc: A prefix is a few letters at the front that change a word's meaning. Twenty of them cover most of what you'll see.

lessons.title: Suffixes and parts of speech
lessons.desc: The ending of a word usually tells you what job it does in a sentence.

lessons.title: Latin roots I
lessons.desc: Well over half of English words trace back to Latin, many of them through French. These twelve roots unlock hundreds of words.

lessons.title: Greek roots I
lessons.desc: Greek roots run science, medicine and technology. Learn these and technical words stop being scary.

units.title: Core Academic Words
units.summary: The words teachers and tests use constantly.

lessons.title: Words for thinking: analyze, infer, evaluate
lessons.desc: The verbs teachers, tests and bosses use when they want you to think, not just remember.

lessons.title: Words for change and cause
lessons.desc: Precise words for how things change and why they happen.

lessons.title: Words for amount and degree
lessons.desc: Ditch "a lot," "very" and "kind of." These words say exactly how much.

lessons.title: Words for people and character
lessons.desc: Describe people precisely: in reviews, hiring, stories and deals.

units.title: Roots II & Word Families
units.summary: More roots, and how one root unlocks dozens of words.

lessons.title: Latin roots II
lessons.desc: Fourteen more Latin roots, the spelling disguises they hide behind, and a method for decoding words you have never seen.

lessons.title: Greek roots II
lessons.desc: The Greek roots behind the words for people, power, feeling and form, plus how scientists still build new words from them.

lessons.title: Word families
lessons.desc: Learn one word and you've learned five. How word families work, why their spelling and sound shift, and how to use the right form every time.

lessons.title: Number and measurement roots
lessons.desc: Latin and Greek counted differently. Learn both systems and every number word, from bicycle to gigabyte to sesquicentennial, becomes obvious.

units.title: Precision
units.summary: Choosing exactly the right word.

lessons.title: Connotation: same meaning, different feel
lessons.desc: Thrifty, frugal, cheap and stingy all mean the same thing, and they'll get you four different reactions. How word choice persuades before the argument even starts.

lessons.title: Shades of meaning
lessons.desc: "The difference between the almost right word and the right word is really a large matter: 'tis the difference between the lightning-bug and the lightning." (Mark Twain)

lessons.title: Commonly confused words
lessons.desc: The pairs that make smart people look careless in emails, contracts and résumés, with a memory trick for each.

lessons.title: Idioms and figurative language
lessons.desc: Metaphor, simile, hyperbole and the idioms English borrowed from the boxing ring, the racetrack and the ballpark. Read between the lines and write with punch.

units.title: High School Power Words
units.summary: Words that make writing and speaking sharper.

units.title: SAT & AP Level
units.summary: Advanced words, words in context and rhetoric vocabulary.

units.title: Words for Business & Money
units.summary: The vocabulary of deals, contracts and markets.

title: Writing
blurb: Clear sentences, strong paragraphs, persuasive essays and real-world writing that gets results.
intro: Good writing is clear thinking on paper. This course goes from sentence mechanics to AP-level rhetorical analysis, with a unit on the writing you actually use: emails, proposals and negotiation.

units.title: Sentences
units.summary: Building complete, correct, punchy sentences.

lessons.title: Subjects, verbs and complete sentences
lessons.desc: Every sentence needs three things. Find them and you can fix almost any sentence.

lessons.title: Fragments and run-ons
lessons.desc: The two most common sentence errors, and the four ways to fix every run-on.

lessons.title: Punctuation essentials
lessons.desc: Apostrophes, colons, semicolons, dashes and quotation marks, with the rules that actually matter.

lessons.title: Commas without guessing
lessons.desc: Six rules cover almost every comma you'll ever need. If none applies, leave it out.

lessons.title: Active voice
lessons.desc: Put the doer first. It's the single easiest way to make writing clearer and stronger.

units.title: Paragraphs
units.summary: Organizing ideas so they land.

lessons.title: Topic sentences
lessons.desc: The first sentence of a paragraph should tell the reader exactly what the paragraph will prove.

lessons.title: Evidence and explanation
lessons.desc: Claims need proof, and proof needs explaining. The C-E-R pattern does both.

lessons.title: Transitions
lessons.desc: Transition words tell the reader how one idea connects to the next.

lessons.title: Concision: cutting the fat
lessons.desc: Say it in fewer words. Every word you cut makes the rest hit harder.

units.title: Grammar for Clarity
units.summary: The grammar rules that change meaning.

lessons.title: Subject-verb agreement
lessons.desc: A verb has to match its subject. The rule takes ten seconds to learn. Finding the real subject is the skill, and this lesson trains it.

lessons.title: Pronouns
lessons.desc: I or me, who or whom, its or it's, he or they: the pronoun choices that make writing sound educated, and the one test that settles almost all of them.

lessons.title: Misplaced modifiers
lessons.desc: A describing word attaches to whatever it's next to. Put it in the wrong spot and your sentence says something absurd, or something you'll have to pay for.

lessons.title: Parallel structure
lessons.desc: Items in a list should match in form. It's the difference between writing that stumbles and writing that hits like a combination.

lessons.title: Verb tense consistency
lessons.desc: Pick a timeline and stay on it. When time really does shift, use the tenses built to show exactly when things happened.

units.title: The Essay
units.summary: Thesis, structure and revision.

lessons.title: Writing a thesis
lessons.desc: One sentence that takes a position, tells the reader what's coming, and gives the whole essay a spine. Most weak essays are weak right here.

lessons.title: Outlining
lessons.desc: An outline is where the thinking happens. Five minutes of structure saves an hour of rewriting, and the right shape makes your argument hit harder.

lessons.title: Introductions and conclusions
lessons.desc: The first lines decide whether anyone keeps reading. The last lines decide what they remember. How to open with a hook and close with a punch.

lessons.title: Revising like an editor
lessons.desc: Good writing is rewritten writing. The order professional editors work in, the cuts they always make, and the tricks for seeing your own mistakes.

units.title: Argument
units.summary: Making a case and taking one apart.

units.title: Real-World Writing
units.summary: The writing that moves money and people.

units.title: AP Language & Composition
units.summary: The three AP essays and the style moves behind them.

title: Science
blurb: How the world works: matter, energy, life, Earth and space, up to AP Biology, Chemistry and Physics.
intro: Science is a way of thinking before it's a pile of facts. The first unit teaches that thinking; the rest apply it from middle-school foundations to AP-level biology, chemistry and physics.

units.title: Thinking Like a Scientist
units.summary: The method, variables, measurement and graphs.

lessons.title: The scientific method
lessons.desc: Science is a method for not fooling yourself. Here's how it works, and what hypothesis, theory and law really mean.

lessons.title: Variables and controls
lessons.desc: How to run a fair test, and why correlation isn't causation.

lessons.title: Measurement and units
lessons.desc: The metric system, the prefixes that make it easy, and the difference between accurate and precise.

lessons.title: Reading graphs and data
lessons.desc: How to read a graph in ten seconds, find the rate in a slope, and catch a misleading chart.

units.title: Matter & Chemistry Basics
units.summary: Atoms, elements and reactions.

lessons.title: Atoms and their parts
lessons.desc: Everything you can touch is made of atoms. Here's what's inside one.

lessons.title: The periodic table
lessons.desc: The periodic table is a map. Once you can read it, you can predict how elements behave.

lessons.title: States of matter
lessons.desc: Solid, liquid, gas: what's really different is how fast the particles move.

lessons.title: Chemical reactions
lessons.desc: Atoms rearrange, nothing is lost, and equations have to balance.

units.title: Physics Foundations
units.summary: Motion, forces, energy, waves and electricity.

lessons.title: Speed, velocity and acceleration
lessons.desc: How fast, which way, and how quickly that's changing. The three ideas that describe every moving thing, from a jab to an 80,000-lb truck.

lessons.title: Forces and Newton's laws
lessons.desc: Three laws, written in 1687, still explain every push, pull, punch and crash. Learn them the way an engineer does.

lessons.title: Energy and its forms
lessons.desc: Energy is never made or destroyed, only moved and changed. Follow it and you can explain a punch, a crash, a power bill and the food on your plate.

lessons.title: Waves, sound and light
lessons.desc: A wave moves energy without moving stuff along with it. One equation, v = f·λ, explains your voice, your Wi-Fi and the color of the sky.

lessons.title: Electricity and circuits
lessons.desc: Voltage pushes, current flows, resistance fights back. Master V = I·R and you can read a battery, size a fuse and check your power bill.

units.title: Life Science
units.summary: Cells, genetics, evolution and the body.

lessons.title: Cells
lessons.desc: Every living thing is built from cells, and each cell runs like a small company: a head office, a power plant, a factory floor and a shipping dock.

lessons.title: DNA and genetics
lessons.desc: A four-letter code, three billion letters long, that builds you. How DNA stores information, how it becomes a body, and how traits pass from parents to kids.

lessons.title: Evolution and natural selection
lessons.desc: Variation, inheritance and a struggle to survive: three ingredients that, over many generations, shaped every living thing. Plus the misconceptions almost everyone has.

lessons.title: Human body systems
lessons.desc: Eleven systems, one machine. How your heart, lungs, muscles, nerves and hormones work together, and what actually happens inside you during a fight.

lessons.title: Ecosystems
lessons.desc: Energy flows one way and matter goes in circles. How living things connect, why there are so few sharks and so much grass, and what happened when pythons hit the Everglades.

units.title: Earth & Space
units.summary: Plates, weather, climate and the cosmos.

units.title: Biology
units.summary: The chemistry of life up to how genes are expressed.

units.title: Chemistry
units.summary: Bonding, the mole, equilibrium and acids.

units.title: Physics
units.summary: Mechanics in depth.
